data.narrative:
Field AI, a Series B AI & Software company founded by Ali Agha and Shayegan Omidshafiei, carries a current post-money valuation of $2.0B after raising $405M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private frontier-tech peers and 1 public reference (Palantir, ticker PLTR), with direct comparables including Scale AI ($29.0B), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B), and Black Forest Labs ($3.2B)—all at Series B stage.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $2.0B last post-money and applying a typical 1.9x multiplier for Series B progression, implies a valuation of $3.8B. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector, same-stage comparables yields a median of $5.6B, with a range spanning $3.2B to $29.0B. The wider range reflects substantial valuation dispersion within the AI & Software cohort at this stage.

Synthesis of both methods supports a triangulated range of $3.2B to $6.4B, with a median of $4.7B. This implies modest upside to the current $2.0B mark under conservative assumptions, but meaningful uncertainty remains. Key drivers of range width are: (1) extreme outlier valuations within peer set (Scale AI at $29.0B), (2) limited stage-matched public comparables, and (3) heterogeneous revenue/growth profiles across frontier-tech peers. Tighter ranges would require greater visibility into Field AI's revenue run-rate and unit economics relative to named peers.
